name: 1 Chronicles
sourceNote: Written freshly, thought for thought, from the oldest Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses (the Masoretic Text with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the Samaritan Pentateuch). © 2026 Jose Santiago. All rights reserved.

verses.text: The line began with Adam.{a} Next came Seth, then Enosh,
then Kenan,{b} Mahalalel and Jared,
then Enoch,{c} Methuselah and Lamech,
and then Noah.{d} Noah’s sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.
Japheth had seven sons, named Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.{e}
Three sons were born to Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath{f} and Togarmah.
From Javan came four: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Rodanim.{g}
Ham had four sons: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.{h}
Cush was the father of Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama and Sabteca. Raama had two sons, Sheba and Dedan.{i}
Nimrod was also a son of Cush. He grew to be the first great warrior on the earth.{j}
From Mizraim came the peoples called the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,{k}
Pathrusim and Casluhim. The Philistines came from the Casluhim. The Caphtorim came from Mizraim too.{l}
Canaan’s oldest son was Sidon. After him came Heth.{m}
The Jebusites, Amorites and Girgashites also came from Canaan,
as did the Hivites, Arkites and Sinites,
the Arvadites, Zemarites and the people of Hamath.{n}
Shem had five sons named Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram. Uz, Hul, Gether and Meshech were counted with them too.{o}
Arpachshad had a son named Shelah. Shelah’s son was Eber.{p}
Eber had two sons. One was called Peleg, because the earth was split up during his lifetime. His brother was called Joktan.{q}
Joktan’s sons were Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,{r}
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,{s}
Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,{t}
Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. These were all sons of Joktan.{u}
So the line went from Shem to Arpachshad, then to Shelah,
then to Eber, Peleg and Reu,{v}
then to Serug, Nahor and Terah,{w}
and then to Abram, who is Abraham.{x}
Abraham had two sons, Isaac and Ishmael.{y}
Here is Ishmael’s family, in order of birth. Nebaioth was born first. Then came Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,{z}
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,{aa}
Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah. These twelve were Ishmael’s sons.{ab}
Abraham also had a secondary wife, Keturah. She gave him six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. Two of Jokshan’s sons were Sheba and Dedan.{ac}
Five sons were born to Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. All of these came from Keturah.{ad}
Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac had two sons, Esau and Israel.{ae}
Five sons were born to Esau. They were named Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam and Korah.{af}
To Eliphaz were born Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam and Kenaz. By Timna he also had Amalek.{ag}
Reuel had four boys: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah.{ah}
The family of Seir included seven sons. They were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer and Dishan.{ai}
Two sons were born to Lotan, Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan’s sister.{aj}
Five sons were born to Shobal, named Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi and Onam. Zibeon had two, Aiah and Anah.{ak}
Anah had a son{al} named Dishon. Four sons were born to Dishon, named Hamran, Eshban, Ithran and Cheran.{am}
Three sons were born to Ezer, named Bilhan, Zaavan and Jaakan. Two were born to Dishan,{an} named Uz and Aran.
Before Israel ever had a king, kings ruled the land of Edom. Here they are. First was Bela son of Beor. His city was called Dinhabah.{ao}
After Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah, took the throne.{ap}
After Jobab died, Husham, from the land of the Temanites, took the throne.{aq}
Husham died next. Then Hadad son of Bedad became king. Hadad beat the Midianites in the land of Moab. His city was called Avith.{ar}
Hadad died, and Samlah from Masrekah ruled after him.{as}
Samlah died, and Shaul from Rehoboth on the River ruled after him.{at}
Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor ruled after him.{au}
When Baal-hanan died, a man named Hadad became king. His city was called Pai. His wife was Mehetabel. She was the daughter of Matred and the granddaughter of Me-zahab.{av}
Then Hadad died too. Edom also had clan chiefs. They were the chiefs of Timna, Aliah and Jetheth,{aw}
the chiefs of Oholibamah, Elah and Pinon,{ax}
the chiefs of Kenaz, Teman and Mibzar,{ay}
and the chiefs of Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.{az}

notes.text: Adam means “human being” and sounds like the Hebrew word for “ground.” Seth means “appointed” (Genesis 4:25). Enosh means “mortal man.” Verses 1-4 follow Genesis 5.
Kenan may mean “smith.” Mahalalel means “praise of God.” Jared means “going down.”
Enoch means “set apart.” Methuselah may mean “man of the spear.” The meaning of Lamech is uncertain.
Noah means “rest” (Genesis 5:29). Shem means “name.” Ham may mean “hot.” Japheth may mean “may he make room” (Genesis 9:27).

Verses 5-23 follow Genesis 10. Most of these names stand for peoples and lands, and most of their meanings are unknown. Madai is Media. Javan is Ionia, the Greeks. Tubal and Meshech were peoples in what is now Turkey.
The Hebrew says Diphath. Genesis 10:3 and some Hebrew copies here say “Riphath.” In Hebrew the letters d and r look alike.
The Hebrew says Rodanim. Genesis 10:4 says “Dodanim.” Rodanim probably means the people of Rhodes. Kittim means the people of Cyprus.
Cush is the land south of Egypt. Mizraim is Egypt. Put is probably Libya. Canaan may mean “low land” or “land of purple.”
These were peoples and places of Arabia and Africa. Sheba and Dedan were in Arabia.
Nimrod may mean “let us rebel.”
The main Septuagint copy does not have verses 11-16 or most of verses 17-23. Names ending in -im are names of peoples. Lehabim may mean the Libyans.
The Pathrusim lived in Pathros, in southern Egypt. The Caphtorim were probably the people of Crete. Compare Genesis 10:14, where the order is a little different.
Sidon may mean “fishing place.” Heth was the ancestor of the Hittites.

These were peoples of Canaan and Syria. Several are named after cities, such as Arka, Arvad and Hamath (“fortress”). The Jebusites were named after Jebus, the old name of Jerusalem. Amorites probably means “westerners.”

Genesis 10:23 lists Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash (Meshech here) as Aram’s sons. Here they are listed with Shem’s sons. Elam was in what is now Iran. Asshur is Assyria. Aram was the ancestor of the Arameans (Syrians).
Shelah means “sprout.” Eber may be linked to the word “Hebrew.”
Peleg means “division.” Joktan may mean “small.”
Hazarmaveth means “yard of death” (Hadramaut in southern Arabia). Jerah means “moon.” The meanings of Almodad and Sheleph are uncertain.
Hadoram may mean “Hadad is lifted up.” Diklah means “palm grove.” The meaning of Uzal is uncertain.
The Hebrew says Ebal. Genesis 10:28 says “Obal.” Abimael means “my father is God.”
Ophir was a land famous for its gold. Havilah may mean “sandy land.”
Reu may mean “friend.”
Serug may mean “branch.” Nahor may mean “snorting.” The meaning of Terah is uncertain.
Abram means “honored father.” Abraham sounds like “father of many” (Genesis 17:5).
Isaac means “he laughs.” Ishmael means “God hears.”
These names follow Genesis 25:13-15. Kedar means “dark.” Mibsam means “sweet smell.”
Mishma means “hearing.” Dumah means “silence.” Massa means “load” or “message.” Hadad is the name of a storm god. Tema, “desert,” was an oasis in Arabia.
Jetur’s family were the Itureans. Kedemah means “toward the east.”
Keturah means “incense.” Zimran may mean “wild goat” or “song.” Midian may mean “fighting.”
Ephah means “darkness.” Epher means “young deer.” Hanoch is the same name as Enoch, “set apart.” Abida means “my father knows.”
Esau may mean “hairy” (Genesis 25:25). Israel means “he struggles with God” (Genesis 32:28).
Eliphaz may mean “my God is fine gold.” Reuel means “friend of God.” Korah means “bald.”

Genesis 36:11-12 says Timna was Eliphaz’s secondary wife and Amalek’s mother. The Hebrew here lists Timna and Amalek among the sons. This follows some Septuagint copies and Genesis. Teman means “south.”
Nahath means “quiet.” Zerah means “dawn.”
Seir means “hairy” or “shaggy,” a hill country covered with trees. Zibeon means “hyena.” Dishon and Dishan mean “mountain goat.” Ezer means “help.”
Hori was the ancestor of the Horites, which may mean “cave people.” Genesis 36:22 spells Homam as Hemam.
Genesis 36:23 spells Alian as Alvan and Shephi as Shepho. Manahath means “rest.” Aiah means “hawk.”
The Hebrew says “sons.”
Genesis 36:26 calls Hamran “Hemdan,” which means “pleasant.” Ithran means “plenty.”
The Hebrew says “Dishon.” Genesis 36:28 says “Dishan.” Genesis 36:27 spells Jaakan as Akan.
Verses 43-54 follow Genesis 36:31-43. Bela means “swallowing up.” The meaning of Dinhabah is uncertain.
Bozrah means “sheep pen” or “fortress.”
Husham may mean “hurry.” The Temanites were “people of the south.”
Bedad may mean “alone.” Avith may mean “ruins.”
Samlah means “robe.” Masrekah may mean “vineyard.”
Shaul means “asked for.” Rehoboth means “wide places.” The River is probably the Euphrates.
Baal-hanan means “the lord (or Baal) is kind.”
Genesis 36:39 says “Hadar” and “Pau” and does not mention his death. Mehetabel means “God does good.” Me-zahab means “waters of gold.”
Genesis 36:40 spells Aliah as Alvah. The meaning of Jetheth is uncertain.
Oholibamah means “tent of the high place.” Elah means “oak.”
Mibzar means “fortress.”
Magdiel means “gift of God.” Iram may mean “city.”

verses.text: Israel had twelve sons. Their names were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,{a}
then Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.{b}
Three of Judah’s sons were born to Bath-shua, a Canaanite woman. They were Er, Onan and Shelah. Er was Judah’s oldest son. Yahweh saw that Er was evil, so Yahweh took his life.{c}
Judah also had two sons, Perez and Zerah, with Tamar, his son’s widow. In all, Judah had five sons.{d}
Perez had two sons, Hezron and Hamul.{e}
Born to Zerah were five: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara.{f}
Achar was a son{g} of Carmi. He brought trouble on Israel, because he kept things that belonged to God and were to be destroyed.{h}
Ethan’s son was Azariah.{i}
Hezron had three sons: Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai.{j}
Ram had a son named Amminadab, and Amminadab had a son named Nahshon. Nahshon was the leader of Judah’s people.{k}
Nahshon’s son was Salma, and Salma’s son was Boaz.{l}
Boaz’s son was Obed, and Obed’s son was Jesse.{m}
Seven sons were born to Jesse. Eliab came first, Abinadab second, Shimea third,{n}
Nethanel fourth and Raddai fifth.{o}
Ozem was sixth, and David was seventh.{p}
Zeruiah and Abigail were their sisters. Born to Zeruiah were three sons: Abishai, Joab and Asahel.{q}
Abigail gave birth to Amasa. Jether the Ishmaelite was his father.{r}
Caleb, Hezron’s son, became a father through Azubah, his wife, and through Jerioth.{s} Born to Jerioth were Jesher, Shobab and Ardon.{t}
After Azubah’s death, Ephrath became Caleb’s wife, and she bore Hur.{u}
Hur’s son was Uri, and Uri’s son was Bezalel.{v}
Hezron was sixty when he took Machir’s daughter as his wife. (Machir was Gilead’s father.) She bore Hezron a son, Segub.{w}
Segub’s son was Jair. Twenty-three towns in Gilead belonged to Jair.{x}
But Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-jair away from them. They also took Kenath and the villages around it, sixty towns in all. All these people were descendants of Machir, Gilead’s father.
Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah. After his death, Abijah, his widow, bore Ashhur. Ashhur became the father of Tekoa.{z}
Jerahmeel was Hezron’s oldest son. Jerahmeel’s sons were Ram, the oldest, then Bunah, Oren, Ozem and Ahijah.{aa}
Atarah was another of Jerahmeel’s wives. Onam was her son.{ab}
Ram, Jerahmeel’s oldest son, had three sons: Maaz, Jamin and Eker.{ac}
Onam had two sons, Shammai and Jada. Shammai’s two sons were Nadab and Abishur.{ad}
Abishur married a woman named Abihail. She had his sons Ahban and Molid.{ae}
Nadab had two sons, Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children when he died.{af}
Appaim had a son,{ag} Ishi. Ishi had a son, Sheshan. Sheshan had a child, Ahlai.
Shammai’s brother Jada had two sons, Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children when he died.{ah}
Born to Jonathan were Peleth and Zaza. This was the family line of Jerahmeel.{ai}
No sons were born to Sheshan, only daughters. One of his servants was an Egyptian. The servant’s name was Jarha.{aj}
Sheshan let Jarha marry one of his daughters, and she bore Attai.{ak}
Attai’s son was Nathan, and Nathan’s son was Zabad.{al}
Zabad’s son was Ephlal, and Ephlal’s son was Obed.{am}
Obed’s son was Jehu, and Jehu’s son was Azariah.{an}
Azariah’s son was Helez, and Helez’s son was Eleasah.{ao}
Eleasah’s son was Sismai, and Sismai’s son was Shallum.{ap}
Shallum’s son was Jekamiah, and Jekamiah’s son was Elishama.{aq}
Caleb was Jerahmeel’s brother. Mesha was Caleb’s firstborn. Mesha founded Ziph. Caleb’s family also included Mareshah, who founded Hebron.{ar}
Born to Hebron were four sons: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem and Shema.{as}
Raham came from Shema, and from Raham came Jorkeam. From Rekem came Shammai.{at}
From Shammai came Maon, and Maon founded Beth-zur.{au}
Ephah, a secondary wife of Caleb, bore Haran, Moza and Gazez. Haran named one of his sons Gazez.{av}
Born to Jahdai were six sons: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah and Shaaph.{aw}
Caleb had another secondary wife, Maacah. She had his sons Sheber and Tirhanah.{ax}
Maacah also bore Shaaph, who founded Madmannah, and Sheva, who founded Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb had a daughter named Achsah.{ay}
That is the list of Caleb’s family. Ephrathah’s oldest son was Hur. Hur had three sons. Shobal started the town of Kiriath-jearim.{az}
Salma started Bethlehem. Hareph started Beth-gader.{ba}
Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, had these descendants: Haroeh and half of the Menuhoth people.{bb}
Kiriath-jearim was home to these clans: the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites and Mishraites. From them came the people of Zorah and of Eshtaol.{bc}
Salma was the ancestor of the people of Bethlehem and the Netophathites. He was also the ancestor of Atroth-beth-joab, of half the Manahathites, and of the Zorites.{bd}
At Jabez lived clans of writers, the Tirathites, Shimeathites and Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the ancestor of Rechab’s family.{be}

notes.text: Reuben means “look, a son.” Simeon means “hearing.” Levi means “joined.” Judah means “praised.” Issachar means “there is a reward.” Zebulun means “honor” or “home” (Genesis 29-30).
Dan means “judge.” Joseph means “may he add.” Benjamin means “son of the right hand.” Naphtali means “my wrestling.” Gad means “good luck.” Asher means “happy.”
Er means “watchful.” Onan means “strength.” Bath-shua means “daughter of Shua” (Genesis 38:2). Compare Genesis 38:7.
Tamar means “palm tree.” Perez means “breaking through.” Zerah means “dawn.”
Hezron may mean “walled yard.” Hamul means “spared.”
The Hebrew says Dara. Some ancient copies and 1 Kings 4:31 say “Darda.” Joshua 7:1 calls Zimri “Zabdi.” Ethan means “lasting.” Heman means “faithful.”
The Hebrew says “sons.”
Achar means “trouble.” Joshua 7:1 calls him Achan. Carmi means “my vineyard.”
Azariah means “Yahweh has helped.”
Jerahmeel means “may God show mercy.” Ram means “high.” Chelubai is another form of Caleb (verse 18).
Amminadab means “my relative is noble.” Nahshon may mean “snake” or “bronze.”
Ruth 4:20-21 spells Salma as Salmah and Salmon. Boaz may mean “in him is strength.”
Obed means “servant” or “worshiper.” The meaning of Jesse is uncertain.
Eliab means “my God is father.” Abinadab means “my father is noble.” Shimea means “hearing.” 1 Samuel 16:9 calls him Shammah.
Nethanel means “God has given.” Raddai may mean “ruling.”
1 Samuel 16:10-11 and 17:12 say Jesse had eight sons, with David the youngest. Chronicles names seven. Some ancient versions add Elihu (compare 27:18). David means “loved one.”
Zeruiah may mean “healing oil.” Abigail means “my father is joy.” Abishai means “my father is a gift.” Joab means “Yahweh is father.” Asahel means “God has made.”
2 Samuel 17:25 calls him Ithra the Israelite. Amasa means “load carrier.” Jether means “plenty.”
Or “fathered Jerioth by his wife Azubah.” The Hebrew is not clear.
Caleb means “dog” or “whole-hearted.” Azubah means “left alone.” Jerioth means “tent curtains.” Jesher means “honesty.” Shobab means “returning.”
Ephrath means “fruitful.” Hur may mean “white linen.”
Uri means “my light.” Bezalel means “in God’s shadow,” that is, under his protection (Exodus 31:2).
Machir means “sold.” Gilead may mean “rough land.” Segub means “lifted high.”
Jair means “he gives light.” Geshur means “bridge.” Havvoth-jair means “villages of Jair.” Kenath means “owned land.”

The Hebrew here is hard to understand. The Septuagint says “after Hezron died, Caleb came to Ephrathah.” Many experts think the text first said that Caleb married Hezron’s widow. Abijah means “Yahweh is my father.” Tekoa means “trumpet blast.” “Father” here may mean the founder or leader of a town.
Bunah means “understanding.” Oren means “pine tree.” Ahijah means “brother of Yahweh.” The Hebrew may mean that Ahijah was one of Jerahmeel’s wives.
Atarah means “crown.” Onam means “strong.”
Maaz means “anger.” Jamin means “right hand.” Eker means “root.”
Jada means “he knows.” Nadab means “generous.” Abishur means “my father is a wall.”
Abihail means “my father is strength.” Molid means “father of children.”
Seled means “joy.” Appaim means “nostrils” or “face.”
The Hebrew says “sons” in this whole verse. Ishi means “my salvation.”
Jonathan means “Yahweh has given.”
Peleth means “speed.” The meaning of Zaza is uncertain.
The meaning of Jarha is uncertain.
Attai means “on time.”
Nathan means “he has given.” Zabad means “gift.”
Ephlal means “judgment.”
Jehu means “Yahweh is he.”
Helez means “strength.” Eleasah means “God has made.”
Shallum means “payment.”
Jekamiah means “may Yahweh raise up.” Elishama means “God has heard.”
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to understand. Mesha means “salvation.” Mareshah means “hilltop.” Hebron means “joining together.”
Tappuah means “apple.” Rekem means “many colors.” Shema means “hearing.”
Raham means “mercy.”
Maon means “home.” Beth-zur means “house of rock.”
Moza means “going out.” Gazez means “sheep shearer.”
Regem means “friend.” Jotham means “Yahweh is perfect.” Pelet means “escape.”
Maacah may mean “pressing down.” Sheber means “breaking.”
Madmannah means “manure pile.” Gibea means “hill.” Achsah means “ankle bracelet” (Joshua 15:16-17).
Ephrathah is the same as Ephrath (verse 19). Kiriath-jearim means “town of forests.”
Bethlehem means “house of bread.” Beth-gader means “house of the wall.”
Or “Reaiah, half of the Manahathites” (compare 4:2 and verse 54). Haroeh means “the seer.” Menuhoth means “resting places.”
The Ithrites came from Jether. Zorah means “hornets.”
The Netophathites came from Netophah (“dripping”). Atroth-beth-joab means “crowns of Joab’s family.”

Or “the gatekeepers, the listeners and the tent dwellers.” The meaning is uncertain. Jabez means “he causes pain” (4:9). Kenites may mean “metalworkers.” Hammath means “hot spring.” Rechab means “rider” (Jeremiah 35).

verses.text: David had sons born to him while he lived at Hebron. Amnon was his firstborn, and Ahinoam from Jezreel was Amnon’s mother. Next came Daniel, whose mother was Abigail from Carmel.{a}
Absalom was third. His mother was Maacah, a daughter of Talmai, Geshur’s king. Adonijah was fourth, and Haggith was his mother.{b}
Shephatiah was fifth, born to Abital. Ithream was sixth, born to Eglah, David’s wife.{c}
So six sons were born to David at Hebron. He ruled from Hebron for seven years and six months. After that he ruled from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.{d}
In Jerusalem four more sons were born to him by Bath-shua, Ammiel’s daughter. They were Shimea, Shobab, Nathan and Solomon.{e}
Nine others were born there too: Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,{f}
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,{g}
Elishama, Eliada and Eliphelet.{h}
All of these were David’s sons. He also had sons by his secondary wives. Tamar was a sister of these sons.{i}
Here is the line of kings that came from Solomon. After Solomon came Rehoboam, then Abijah, then Asa, then Jehoshaphat,{j}
then Joram, Ahaziah and Joash,{k}
then Amaziah, Azariah and Jotham,{l}
then Ahaz, Hezekiah and Manasseh,{m}
then Amon, and then Josiah. Each was the son of the king before him.{n}
Josiah had four sons. Johanan was born first, Jehoiakim second, Zedekiah third, and Shallum fourth.{o}
Jehoiakim was the father of Jeconiah, and Jeconiah was the father of Zedekiah.{p}
Jeconiah was taken captive.{q} His first son was Shealtiel.{r}
After him came Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama and Nedabiah.{s}
From Pedaiah came Zerubbabel and Shimei. From Zerubbabel came Meshullam and Hananiah, and a daughter, Shelomith.{t}
Zerubbabel also had five more sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah and Jushab-hesed.{u}
From Hananiah came Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The families of Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah and Shecaniah came from him too.{v}
Shecaniah had a son{w} named Shemaiah. Six were born to Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah and Shaphat.{x}
Three were born to Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam.{y}
Seven were born to Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah and Anani.{z}

notes.text: 2 Samuel 3:3 calls the second son Chileab. Amnon means “faithful.” Ahinoam means “my brother is pleasant.” Jezreel means “God plants.” Daniel means “God is my judge.” Carmel means “garden land.”
Absalom means “father of peace.” Adonijah means “my lord is Yahweh.” Haggith means “festival.”
Shephatiah means “Yahweh has judged.” Abital means “my father is dew.” Ithream means “rest of the people.” Eglah means “young cow.”
Compare 2 Samuel 5:4-5.

Bath-shua, “daughter of Shua,” is Bathsheba (2 Samuel 11:3). Ammiel, “my relative is God,” is Eliam, with the two parts of the name turned around. 2 Samuel 5:14 calls Shimea “Shammua.” Solomon means “peaceful.”
Ibhar means “he chooses.” 2 Samuel 5:15 calls this Elishama “Elishua.” Eliphelet means “God rescues.” This Eliphelet and Nogah (verse 7) are not in 2 Samuel 5:14-16. Compare 14:5-6.
Nogah means “brightness.” Nepheg means “sprout.” Japhia means “he shines.”
Eliada means “God knows.” Compare 14:7, where he is called Beeliada. The Hebrew adds “nine.”
Tamar means “palm tree” (2 Samuel 13).
Rehoboam means “the people grow.” 1 Kings 15:1 calls Abijah “Abijam.” Asa may mean “healer.” Jehoshaphat means “Yahweh has judged.”
Joram, also called Jehoram, means “Yahweh is lifted up.” Ahaziah means “Yahweh has grasped.” Joash may mean “Yahweh has given.”
Amaziah means “Yahweh is mighty.” Azariah is also called Uzziah (2 Chronicles 26).
Ahaz means “he has grasped.” Hezekiah means “Yahweh makes strong.” Manasseh means “making to forget.”
Amon means “faithful” or “skilled worker.” Josiah means “Yahweh supports.”
Johanan means “Yahweh is kind.” Jehoiakim means “Yahweh raises up.” Zedekiah means “Yahweh is righteous.” Shallum is Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:30-31; Jeremiah 22:11).
Jeconiah means “Yahweh makes firm.” He is also called Jehoiachin and Coniah. This Zedekiah seems to have been Jeconiah’s son. 2 Kings 24:17 calls a Zedekiah Jehoiachin’s uncle.
Or “Jeconiah: Assir.” The Hebrew word assir means “captive,” and it may also be read as a name.
Shealtiel means “I asked God.”
Malchiram means “my king is lifted up.” Pedaiah means “Yahweh has set free.” Shenazzar is a Babylonian name. Hoshama means “Yahweh has heard.” Nedabiah means “Yahweh is generous.”

Other books call Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel (Ezra 3:2; Haggai 1:1). Here he is called the son of Pedaiah, who may have been Shealtiel’s brother. Zerubbabel means “child of Babylon.” Hananiah means “Yahweh is kind.” Shelomith means “peaceful.”
Ohel means “tent.” Berechiah means “Yahweh blesses.” Hasadiah means “Yahweh is kind.” Jushab-hesed means “kindness is returned.”

The Hebrew is not clear. The Septuagint says “Rephaiah was his son, then Arnan, then Obadiah, then Shecaniah.” Pelatiah means “Yahweh rescues.” Jeshaiah means “Yahweh saves.” Rephaiah means “Yahweh heals.” Obadiah means “servant of Yahweh.” Shecaniah means “Yahweh lives with us.”
The Hebrew says “sons.”
The Hebrew says six, but only five names are listed. One may have been lost. Shemaiah means “Yahweh hears.” Igal means “he sets free.” Neariah means “young man of Yahweh.” Shaphat means “he judges.”
Elioenai means “my eyes look to Yahweh.” Hizkiah is a form of Hezekiah. Azrikam means “my help has come.”
Hodaviah means “give thanks to Yahweh.” Eliashib means “God brings back.” Pelaiah means “Yahweh is wonderful.” Delaiah means “Yahweh has drawn out.” Anani means “my cloud.”

verses.text: Judah’s family line includes Perez, then Hezron, Carmi, Hur and Shobal.{a}
Reaiah, a son of Shobal, fathered Jahath. Born to Jahath were Ahumai and Lahad. The Zorathite clans came from them.{b}
These were the sons{c} of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma and Idbash. They had a sister called Hazzelelponi.{d}
Penuel founded Gedor, and Ezer founded Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, Ephrathah’s firstborn, who founded Bethlehem.{e}
Ashhur, who founded Tekoa, was married to two women, Helah and Naarah.{f}
Naarah bore four of his sons: Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni and Haahashtari.{g}
Helah bore three: Zereth, Izhar{h} and Ethnan.{i}
Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah. The clans of Aharhel son of Harum also came from Koz.{j}
Jabez was honored more than his brothers. His mother had named him Jabez. “Giving birth to him hurt me so much,” she said.{k}

Jabez cried out to Israel’s God. “Please bless me greatly,” he prayed. “Give me more land. Stay with me and keep your hand on me. Protect me from harm, so I will be free from pain.” And God answered his prayer.
Chelub, Shuhah’s brother, fathered Mehir, and Mehir fathered Eshton.{l}
From Eshton came Beth-rapha, Paseah and Tehinnah. Tehinnah founded Ir-nahash. These were the people of Recah.{m}
Two sons were born to Kenaz, Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel’s sons were Hathath{n} and Meonothai.{o}
Ophrah’s father was Meonothai. Seraiah was Joab’s father, and Joab started the settlement of Ge-harashim.{p} It got its name because its people were skilled workers.{q}
From Caleb, Jephunneh’s son, came Iru, Elah and Naam. Elah’s son{r} was Kenaz.{s}
Four were born to Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria and Asarel.{t}
Four were born to Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher and Jalon. Mered’s wife{u} became the mother of Miriam, Shammai and Ishbah. Ishbah founded Eshtemoa.{v}

Mered also had a wife from Judah. She bore Jered, the founder of Gedor, Heber, the founder of Soco, and Jekuthiel, the founder of Zanoah. Mered had married Bithiah, a daughter of Pharaoh, and these were her sons.{w}
Hodiah married Naham’s sister. One of her sons founded Keilah and was called the Garmite. Another was Eshtemoa the Maacathite.{x}
Shimon’s four sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan and Tilon. Ishi’s two sons were Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.{y}
Shelah, a son of Judah, was the ancestor of these: Er, who founded Lecah; Laadah, who founded Mareshah; and the clans who made fine linen at Beth-ashbea.{z}
So did Jokim, the people of Cozeba, Joash and Saraph. Joash and Saraph ruled in Moab and then came back to Lehem.{aa} These records are very old.
These men made pottery. Netaim and Gederah{ab} were their homes, and there they did the king’s work.
From Simeon came five sons, named Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah and Shaul.{ac}
Next in Simeon’s line came Shallum, son of Shaul, and then Mibsam and Mishma.{ad}
Mishma’s line went on through Hammuel, then Zaccur, then Shimei.{ae}
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters. But his brothers had few children. So their whole clan never grew as large as Judah’s.
Beersheba was one of their towns. Moladah and Hazar-shual{af} were too.
So were Bilhah, Ezem and Tolad,{ag}
Bethuel, Hormah and Ziklag,{ah}
along with Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri and Shaaraim. These towns were theirs until David’s time as king.{ai}
Five more towns were theirs too: Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen and Ashan.{aj}
The villages near these towns were theirs too, all the way to Baal. These were their homes, and they kept a written record of their families.{ak}
Some of their leaders were Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,{al}
Joel, and Jehu, whose father was Joshibiah, whose grandfather was Seraiah, and whose great-grandfather was Asiel.{am}
Others were Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel and Benaiah,{an}
and Ziza. Ziza’s father was Shiphi, then came Allon, Jedaiah, Shimri and Shemaiah, each the father of the one before.{ao}
Those named here were leaders of their clans. Their families grew very large.
They went to the edge of Gedor,{ap} east of the valley, looking for grassland for their sheep and goats.
They found rich, green pastures there. The land was wide open, peaceful and quiet. Some of Ham’s descendants had lived there before.

These leaders came in the days of Hezekiah, Judah’s king. They attacked the tents of Ham’s people and the Meunites{aq} who lived there. They wiped them out completely, and nobody lives there from those peoples to this day. Then the Simeonites settled there, because there was grass for their flocks.
Five hundred Simeonite men went to the hills of Seir. Ishi’s four sons, Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah and Uzziel, were their commanders.{ar}
There they struck down the Amalekites who were left, those who had gotten away before. Simeon’s people have lived there ever since.

notes.text: Here “sons” means descendants over many generations. See chapter 2 for these names.
Reaiah means “Yahweh has seen.” Lahad may mean “pressure.” For the Zorathites, see 2:53.
The Septuagint says “sons.” The Hebrew says “father.”
Etam means “place of birds of prey.” Ishma may mean “he hears.” Idbash means “sweet as honey.” Hazzelelponi may mean “give shade, you who turn to me.”
Penuel means “face of God.” Gedor means “wall.” Hushah means “hurry.” For Hur and Ephrathah, see 2:19 and 2:50.
For Ashhur and Tekoa, see 2:24. Helah may mean “jewelry.” Naarah means “girl.”
Ahuzzam means “property.” Hepher means “well.” Temeni means “southerner.” Haahashtari may be a clan name.
The Hebrew read aloud says Izhar, “he shines.” The written Hebrew says “Zohar,” “whiteness.”
Ethnan means “gift.”
Koz means “thorn.” Anub may mean “grape.” Harum means “lifted up.”
Jabez sounds like the Hebrew word for “pain,” with two letters switched. The Septuagint ends verse 10 with “that you would make me know that you will not bring me grief.”
Chelub means “basket,” or it may be a form of Caleb. Mehir means “price.”

The Septuagint says “the city of Naas, the brother of Eselom the Kenizzite” and “men of Rechab.” Beth-rapha means “house of a giant” or “house of healing.” Paseah means “limping.” Tehinnah means “prayer for help.” Ir-nahash means “snake town.”
The main Septuagint copy gives only Hathath. Other Greek copies and the Latin Vulgate add “and Meonothai,” and verse 14 seems to expect it.
Othniel may mean “lion of God.” Seraiah means “Yahweh is prince.” Hathath means “terror.” Meonothai means “my homes.”
Ge-harashim means “valley of craftsmen” (Nehemiah 11:35).
Ophrah means “young deer.”
The Hebrew says “sons.”
Jephunneh may mean “he will be turned.” Naam means “pleasant.” The Hebrew of the end of the verse says “and Kenaz.” The meaning is uncertain.
Jehallelel means “he praises God.” Ziphah is the female form of Ziph.
The Hebrew says “she.” The second part of verse 18 seems to belong here, which would make Bithiah the mother.
Ezrah means “help.” Mered means “rebellion.” Miriam may mean “loved.” Ishbah means “he praises.” Eshtemoa may mean “I will make myself heard.”

Or “his wife Jehudijah.” Heber means “friend.” Soco means “branches.” Jekuthiel may mean “God will feed.” Bithiah means “daughter of Yahweh.” Pharaoh was the title of Egypt’s king. It means “great house.”
Hodiah means “glory of Yahweh.” Naham means “comfort.” Keilah may mean “fortress.”
Rinnah means “shout of joy.” Ben-hanan means “son of the kind one.” Ben-zoheth means “son of Zoheth.”
Lecah means “walking.” Beth-ashbea means “house of Ashbea.”

Or “who married into Moab and returned to Lehem.” The Hebrew is hard to understand. Jokim means “Yahweh raises up.” Cozeba means “lying.” Saraph means “burning.” Lehem means “bread,” and may mean Bethlehem.
Or “who lived among gardens and walls.” Netaim means “plants.” Gederah means “sheep pen” or “wall.”
Genesis 46:10 and Exodus 6:15 list Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar and Shaul. Jarib means “he argues.”
For Mibsam and Mishma, see 1:29-30.
Hammuel may mean “God is my relative.” Zaccur means “remembered.”
These towns follow Joshua 19:2-8. Beersheba means “well of seven” or “well of the promise.” Moladah means “birth.” Hazar-shual means “fox village.”
Joshua 19:3 spells Bilhah as Balah. Ezem means “bone.” Joshua 19:4 calls Tolad “Eltolad.”
Joshua 19:4 calls Bethuel “Bethul.” Hormah means “set apart for destruction.” The meaning of Ziklag is uncertain.
Beth-marcaboth means “house of chariots.” Hazar-susim means “horse village.” Joshua 19:6 has Beth-lebaoth for Beth-biri and Sharuhen for Shaaraim, which means “two gates.”
Ain means “spring.” Rimmon means “pomegranate.” Joshua 19:7 has Ether for Tochen. Ashan means “smoke.”
Baal means “lord” or “master” (Joshua 19:8 Baalath-beer).
Meshobab means “brought back.” Jamlech means “he makes king.” Joshah means “Yahweh’s gift.”
Joel means “Yahweh is God.” Joshibiah means “Yahweh gives a home.” Asiel means “God has made.”
Jaakobah is a form of Jacob. Asaiah means “Yahweh has made.” Adiel means “jewel of God.” Benaiah means “Yahweh has built.”
Shiphi means “plenty.” Allon means “oak.” Jedaiah means “Yahweh knows.” Shimri means “my guard.”
The Septuagint says “Gerara,” that is, Gerar.
The Hebrew read aloud says Meunites, a people perhaps linked to Maon. The written Hebrew could be read “homes.” The Septuagint says “Minaeans.”
Uzziel means “God is my strength.”

verses.text: Reuben was Israel’s firstborn son. But he slept with one of his father’s wives and so brought shame on his father’s bed. Because of that, his rights as firstborn were handed to the sons of Joseph, Israel’s son. That is why the family lists do not put Reuben first by birth.{a}
Judah grew stronger than his brothers, and a ruler{b} came from his family. Still, the firstborn’s rights went to Joseph.
Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.{c}
Joel’s family line went from Shemaiah to Gog to Shimei,{d}
then to Micah, Reaiah and Baal,{e}
and then to Beerah. Among the Reubenites Beerah was a chief. Tilgath-pilneser, Assyria’s king, carried him away as a captive.{f}
Beerah’s relatives were listed by clan in the family records. Jeiel was their leader. Zechariah was one of them too,{g}
and so was Bela. Bela was the son of Azaz, the grandson of Shema, and the great-grandson of Joel. They lived in Aroer. Their land went north to Nebo and Baal-meon.{h}
Eastward they settled all the way to where the desert begins, the desert that runs to the Euphrates River. They needed the room, because their herds of cattle in Gilead had grown so large.
While Saul was king, they went to war against the Hagrites and beat them. Then they took over the Hagrites’ tents and lived in them all through the land east of Gilead.{i}
Next to Reuben’s tribe, in the land of Bashan, lived the tribe of Gad. Their land went all the way to Salecah.{j}
Joel was their leader, and Shapham was next in rank. Janai and Shaphat were in Bashan too.{k}
Their relatives were listed by families. There were seven of them: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia and Eber.{l} All of them
came from Abihail. Going back from Abihail, his ancestors were Huri, Jaroah, Gilead and Michael, then Jeshishai, Jahdo and Buz.{m}
The head of their family was Ahi. Ahi’s father was Abdiel, and his grandfather was Guni.{n}
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and the towns around it, and in all the grazing land of Sharon, all the way to its borders.{o}
These names were recorded in the family lists during the time of Jotham, Judah’s king, and of Jeroboam, Israel’s king.{p}
Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 brave men ready for war. They were trained for war. Each could handle a shield and a sword and shoot a bow. They were ready for battle.
They fought the Hagrites, and also Jetur, Naphish and Nodab.{q}

God helped them in the fight. He gave the Hagrites and everyone fighting on their side into their power. In the middle of the battle they called to God for help, and he answered them, because they trusted in him.
They took the Hagrites’ animals: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep and 2,000 donkeys. They led away 100,000 prisoners as well.{r}
Many enemy soldiers were killed, because the war was God’s war. The Israelites lived in that land until they were taken away as captives.
Half the tribe of Manasseh lived in that area. They grew to be very many. They spread from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir and Mount Hermon.{s}
Their family leaders were these: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah and Jahdiel. They were strong fighters and famous men, each one the leader of his family.{t}

But the God their fathers had served was not the one they stayed true to. Like an unfaithful wife, they ran after the gods of the peoples of the land. Yet God had destroyed those peoples ahead of them.

So Israel’s God stirred up the mind of Pul, Assyria’s king, who is also called Tilgath-pilneser. He carried the people of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh away as captives. He took them to Halah, Habor and Hara and to the Gozan River. They live there to this day.{u}

notes.text: Or “a leader.” The Hebrew word is nagid.
Pallu means “famous.”
The meaning of Gog is uncertain. The Hebrew does not say how Joel was related to Reuben.
Micah means “who is like Yahweh?”
Tilgath-pilneser is how Chronicles spells Tiglath-pileser (2 Kings 15:29). He ruled Assyria from about 745 to 727 B.C. Beerah means “well.”
Jeiel may mean “God lives.” Zechariah means “Yahweh remembers.”
Azaz means “strong.” Aroer may mean “juniper bush.” Nebo is the name of a god (Nabu). Baal-meon means “lord of the home.”
The Hagrites were a people east of the Jordan, perhaps named after Hagar (Genesis 16). The Septuagint says “foreigners” here and “Agarenes” in verse 19.
Bashan may mean “rich farmland.” The meaning of Salecah is uncertain.
Shapham may mean “bold.” Janai means “he answers.”
Michael means “who is like God?” Jorai may mean “Yahweh teaches.” Zia means “movement.”
Huri means “linen worker.” Jeshishai means “old.” Buz means “scorn.”
Ahi means “my brother.” Abdiel means “servant of God.”
This Sharon, “plain,” was east of the Jordan, not the plain by the sea.
Jotham ruled Judah from about 750 to 735 B.C. Jeroboam II ruled Israel from about 793 to 753 B.C.
Nodab means “noble.”
The Hebrew says “souls of men.” The main Septuagint copy says “5,000 camels.”
Baal-hermon means “lord of Hermon.” Senir was the Amorite name for Hermon (Deuteronomy 3:9). Hermon means “holy mountain.”
Eliel means “my God is God.” Azriel means “God is my help.” Jeremiah means “Yahweh lifts up.” Jahdiel means “God makes glad.”

Or “Pul, Assyria’s king, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser.” Pul was the Babylonian royal name of Tiglath-pileser III (compare 2 Kings 15:19, 29). Halah, Habor and Gozan were in northern Mesopotamia (2 Kings 17:6). The location of Hara is uncertain.

verses.text: Three sons were born to Levi. Their names were Gershon, Kohath and Merari.{a}
Born to Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, four sons in all.{b}
Amram became the father of Aaron and Moses, and of their sister Miriam. Born to Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.{c}
From Eleazar came Phinehas, and from Phinehas came Abishua.{d}
From Abishua came Bukki, and from Bukki came Uzzi.{e}
From Uzzi came Zerahiah, and from Zerahiah came Meraioth.{f}
From Meraioth came Amariah, and from Amariah came Ahitub.{g}
From Ahitub came Zadok, and from Zadok came Ahimaaz.{h}
From Ahimaaz came Azariah, and from Azariah came Johanan.
From Johanan came Azariah. He was the priest who served in the temple Solomon built in Jerusalem.{i}
From Azariah came Amariah, and from Amariah came Ahitub.
From Ahitub came Zadok, and from Zadok came Shallum.
From Shallum came Hilkiah, and from Hilkiah came Azariah.{j}
From Azariah came Seraiah, and from Seraiah came Jehozadak.{k}
Jehozadak was taken away as a captive when Yahweh used Nebuchadnezzar to carry off the people of Judah and Jerusalem.{l}
Levi’s three sons, once again, were Gershom, Kohath and Merari.{m}
Gershom was the father of two boys, named Libni and Shimei.{n}
Born to Kohath were four boys: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
Merari had two sons, Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans, listed by their ancestors.{o}
Gershom’s line went through Libni, then Jahath, then Zimmah,{p}
then Joah, Iddo, Zerah and Jeatherai.{q}
Kohath’s line went through Amminadab, then Korah, then Assir,{r}
then Elkanah, Ebiasaph and Assir,{s}
then Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah and Shaul.{t}
Elkanah’s sons were Amasai and Ahimoth.{u}
Next in Elkanah’s line{v} came Zophai, then Nahath,{w}
then Eliab, Jeroham and Elkanah.{x}
Joel{y} was Samuel’s oldest son, and Abijah was born after him.{z}
Merari’s line went through Mahli, then Libni, Shimei and Uzzah,{aa}
then Shimea, Haggiah and Asaiah.{ab}
After the ark came to rest in Yahweh’s house, David put certain men in charge of the music there.{ac}
They led the singing before the sacred tent where God met with his people, until Solomon built Yahweh’s temple in Jerusalem. They did their work following the rules set for them.
These are the men who served, each with his sons. Heman the singer belonged to the Kohathite clan. Heman’s father was Joel, and Joel’s father was Samuel.{ad}
Before them came Elkanah, Jeroham, Eliel and Toah,{ae}
Zuph, Elkanah, Mahath and Amasai,{af}
Elkanah, Joel, Azariah and Zephaniah,{ag}
Tahath, Assir, Ebiasaph and Korah,
Izhar, Kohath, Levi and Israel. Each was the father of the one listed before him.
Heman’s relative Asaph stood at his right side. Asaph’s father was Berechiah, and before him came Shimea, then{ah}
Michael, then Baaseiah, then Malchijah,{ai}
then Ethni, Zerah and Adaiah,{aj}
then Ethan, then Zimmah and Shimei,
then Jahath, then Gershom, and at the start, Levi.
At Heman’s left side stood their relatives from Merari’s clan. Their leader was Ethan. Ethan’s father was Kishi. Before Kishi came Abdi, then Malluch,{ak}
then Hashabiah, then Amaziah and Hilkiah,{al}
then Amzi, then Bani and Shemer,{am}
then Mahli and Mushi, then Merari, and at the start, Levi.
All the other tasks at the holy tent, God’s house, were handed to the rest of the Levites.

Aaron and his descendants were the ones who burned offerings on the altar for burnt offerings and burned incense on the incense altar. They handled every duty in the Most Holy Place. Through their offerings, Israel’s sins were taken away. They did everything just as Moses, God’s servant, had commanded.
Here is Aaron’s line: Eleazar, then Phinehas, then Abishua,
then Bukki, Uzzi and Zerahiah,
then Meraioth, Amariah and Ahitub,
then Zadok and Ahimaaz.
Here are the places where Aaron’s descendants lived, inside the borders of their land.{an} The Kohathite clan received the first share, chosen by lot.
They were given Hebron in Judah, with the grasslands around it.
But the fields and villages around the city went to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
So Aaron’s descendants received Hebron, a city of safety. They also received Libnah, Jattir and Eshtemoa,{ao}
Hilen and Debir,{ap}
Ashan and Beth-shemesh. Each town came with its grasslands.{aq}
From Benjamin’s tribe they received Geba, Alemeth and Anathoth, each with its grasslands. In all, thirteen towns went to their clans.{ar}
The rest of Kohath’s descendants were given ten towns, chosen by lot, from the clans of half the tribe of Manasseh.{as}
Gershom’s descendants, clan by clan, received thirteen towns. These came from Issachar, Asher and Naphtali, and from Manasseh’s land in Bashan.
Merari’s descendants, clan by clan, received twelve towns by lot. These came from the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun.
So the people of Israel handed over these towns, with the grasslands around them, to the Levite clans.
The towns named here were given out by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon and Benjamin.
Some of Kohath’s clans received towns from Ephraim’s tribe.
They were given Shechem, a city of safety in the hills of Ephraim, and also Gezer,{at}
Jokmeam, Beth-horon,{au}
Aijalon and Gath-rimmon. Each town came with its grasslands.{av}
From half the tribe of Manasseh, the other Kohathite clans received Aner and Bileam, with their grasslands.{aw}
From half of Manasseh’s tribe, Gershom’s descendants received Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, with their grasslands.{ax}
From Issachar’s tribe they received Kedesh, Daberath,{ay}
Ramoth and Anem, with their grasslands.{az}
From Asher’s tribe they received Mashal, Abdon,{ba}
Hukok and Rehob, with their grasslands.{bb}
Naphtali’s tribe gave them Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon and Kiriathaim, each with grasslands.{bc}
The rest of Merari’s descendants received towns from Zebulun’s tribe: Rimmono and Tabor, with their grasslands.{bd}
From Reuben’s tribe, on the east side of the Jordan River across from Jericho, they received Bezer in the desert, and Jahzah,{be}
Kedemoth and Mephaath, with their grasslands.{bf}
From Gad’s tribe they received Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim,{bg}
Heshbon and Jazer, with their grasslands.{bh}

notes.text: In Hebrew, verses 1-15 are 5:27-41, and verses 16-81 are 6:1-66. Gershon, also spelled Gershom (verse 16), may mean “a foreigner there” (Exodus 2:22). Kohath may mean “gathering.” Merari means “bitter.”
Amram means “honored people.” Izhar means “shining oil.”

The meaning of Aaron is uncertain. Moses means “pulled out” (Exodus 2:10), and it is probably also an Egyptian word for “son.” Abihu means “he is my father.” Eleazar means “God has helped.” Ithamar may mean “island of palms.”
Phinehas is an Egyptian name meaning “the Nubian.” Abishua means “my father is salvation.”
Uzzi means “my strength.”
Zerahiah means “Yahweh has dawned.” Meraioth means “rebellious.”
Amariah means “Yahweh has spoken.” Ahitub means “my brother is good.”
Zadok means “righteous.” The meaning of Ahimaaz is uncertain.
This note may belong to the Azariah of verse 9, who was Solomon’s priest (1 Kings 4:2). This list also leaves out some known priests, such as Jehoiada (2 Kings 11) and Uriah (2 Kings 16:10).
Hilkiah means “Yahweh is my share” (2 Kings 22).
Jehozadak means “Yahweh is righteous.” See 2 Kings 25:18 for Seraiah.
This happened in 586 B.C.
This is 6:1 in Hebrew.
Libni means “white.”
Mahli may mean “sick” or “clever.” Mushi may mean “giving way.”
Zimmah means “plan.”
Joah means “Yahweh is brother.” Iddo may mean “on time.” The meaning of Jeatherai is uncertain.
Amminadab here seems to be another name for Izhar (verses 2, 38). Assir means “prisoner.” Compare Exodus 6:21-24, where Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph are Korah’s sons.
Elkanah means “God has created.” Exodus 6:24 spells Ebiasaph as Abiasaph, “my father has gathered.”
Tahath means “below.” Uriel means “God is my light.”
Amasai means “load carrier.” Ahimoth means “my brother is death” (compare Mahath, verse 35).
The Hebrew at the start of this verse is hard to understand. Compare verses 34-35.
Zophai, called Zuph in verse 35, means “honeycomb.” Nahath is called Toah in verse 34.
Eliab is called Eliel in verse 34. Jeroham means “he is shown mercy.” The text may have lost the words “Samuel his son” (compare verse 28 and 1 Samuel 1:1, 20).

The name Joel is added from verse 33 and 1 Samuel 8:2, as in some ancient versions. The Hebrew says “the firstborn Vashni,” which may be read “and the second.” Samuel may mean “name of God” or “heard by God” (1 Samuel 1:20).
The main Septuagint copy says “Sani the firstborn, and Abia.”
Uzzah means “strength.”
Haggiah means “Yahweh’s festival.”
See 2 Samuel 6:17.
This is 6:18 in Hebrew. This Heman is a different man from the one in 2:6.
Toah means “humble.” Compare verses 26-27.
Mahath means “grabbing.”
Zephaniah means “Yahweh has hidden.”
Asaph means “he gathers.”
Baaseiah may mean “work of Yahweh.” Malchijah means “my king is Yahweh.”
Ethni means “gift.” Adaiah means “Yahweh has made beautiful.”
This Ethan is also called Jeduthun (16:41; 25:1). Kishi, called Kushaiah in 15:17, means “trapper.” Abdi means “my servant.” Malluch means “adviser.”
Hashabiah means “Yahweh has counted.”
Amzi means “my strength.” Bani means “built.” Shemer means “guard.”
Verses 54-81 match Joshua 21:10-39, but many names are different. The Hebrew word for “places” can also mean “camps.”
Libnah means “whiteness.” Jattir means “plenty.” In Joshua 21:13 only Hebron among these is a city of safety. The Hebrew here says “cities of safety,” which may be a general way of speaking.
Joshua 21:15 calls Hilen “Holon,” meaning “sand.” Debir means “back room.”
Joshua 21:16 calls Ashan “Ain.” Beth-shemesh means “house of the sun.” Joshua 21:16 also lists Juttah.

Joshua 21:17-18 includes Gibeon and calls Alemeth “Almon.” Geba means “hill.” Alemeth means “covering.” Anathoth comes from the name of the goddess Anath. The number thirteen means two towns are missing from this list.
Joshua 21:5 says “from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan, and from half the tribe of Manasseh.” The Hebrew here seems to be missing the first part.
Joshua 21:21 names only Shechem as a city of safety. Shechem means “shoulder.” Ephraim means “doubly fruitful.” Gezer means “share.”
Joshua 21:22 calls Jokmeam “Kibzaim.” Beth-horon means “house of the hollow.”
Joshua 21:23-24 adds Eltekeh and Gibbethon from Dan. Aijalon means “place of deer.” Gath-rimmon means “pomegranate winepress.”
Joshua 21:25 has Taanach for Aner and Gath-rimmon for Bileam. Bileam may be a form of Ibleam.
Golan may mean “circle.” Ashtaroth (Joshua 21:27 Be-eshterah) is named after the goddess Astarte.
Joshua 21:28 has Kishion for Kedesh. Kedesh means “holy place.” Daberath means “pasture.”
Joshua 21:29 has Jarmuth for Ramoth, which means “heights,” and En-gannim for Anem.
Joshua 21:30 spells Mashal as Mishal. Abdon means “servant.”
Joshua 21:31 has Helkath for Hukok. Rehob means “open place.”
Galilee means “circle” or “district.” Joshua 21:32 has Hammoth-dor for Hammon and Kartan for Kiriathaim, which means “two cities.”
Joshua 21:34-35 lists Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah and Nahalal. Joshua 19:13 spells Rimmono as Rimmon. Tabor means “height.”
Some Hebrew copies of Joshua do not have these verses (Joshua 21:36-37). Jericho may mean “moon city.” Jordan means “flowing down.” Bezer means “fortress.”
Kedemoth means “eastern places.” Mephaath means “brightness.”
Mahanaim means “two camps” (Genesis 32:2).
Heshbon means “counting.” Jazer means “he helps.”

verses.text: Four sons were born to Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron.{a}
From Tola came six sons: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Shemuel. Each led a family in Tola’s clan, and they were strong fighters. In David’s day, Tola’s people counted 22,600 men.{b}
Uzzi had a son named Izrahiah. Born to Izrahiah were four boys: Michael, Obadiah, Joel and Isshiah. Counting their father, all five were leaders.{c}
Because these men had many wives and children, their families could send 36,000 soldiers into war.
Counting every clan in Issachar, the family records listed 87,000 strong fighters.
Three sons were born to Benjamin: Bela, Becher and Jediael.{d}
From Bela came five sons: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth and Iri. They led their families and were brave in battle. Their records counted 22,034 fighting men.{e}
Becher’s family included Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth and Alemeth. All of them were his sons.{f}
Their records, family by family, listed 20,200 brave fighters along with their leaders.
Jediael had a son named Bilhan. Born to Bilhan were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar.{g}
These descendants of Jediael led their families. They had 17,200 strong men ready to march out to war.
Shuppim and Huppim came from Ir, and Hushim came from Aher.{h}
Jahziel, Guni, Jezer and Shallum were born to Naphtali. Their family came through Bilhah.{i}
Manasseh’s family: His concubine from Aram gave birth to Asriel. She also gave birth to Machir, who became Gilead’s father.{j}
Machir took wives for Huppim and Shuppim. Machir’s sister was named Maacah. Another of Manasseh’s descendants, Zelophehad, had only daughters.{k}
Machir’s wife Maacah had a baby boy and named him Peresh. Peresh had a brother named Sheresh. Sheresh’s sons were Ulam and Rakem.{l}
Ulam had a son named Bedan. These all belonged to the family of Gilead, Machir’s son and Manasseh’s grandson.{m}
Gilead’s sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer and Mahlah.{n}
Ahian, Shechem, Likhi and Aniam were the four boys born to Shemida.{o}
Ephraim’s line went from Shuthelah to Bered, then to Tahath, then Eleadah, then another Tahath,{p}

then Zabad, then another Shuthelah. Ephraim also had sons named Ezer and Elead. They went down to steal cattle from the men of Gath, who had been born in that land, and the men of Gath killed them.{q}
Ephraim mourned for them many days. His relatives came to help him through his sorrow.
Afterward Ephraim lay with his wife again, and she gave birth to a baby boy. He called the boy Beriah, because disaster had fallen on his family.{r}
Sheerah, a daughter of Ephraim, founded Lower Beth-horon and Upper Beth-horon, as well as Uzzen-sheerah.{s}
Ephraim’s line also went through Rephah and Resheph, then Telah and Tahan,{t}
then Ladan, Ammihud and Elishama,{u}
then Nun, and then Nun’s son Joshua.{v}

The land and towns where they lived included Bethel with the villages near it. On the east side was Naaran, and on the west was Gezer with its villages. They also had Shechem and Ayyah, each with the villages around it.{w}
Along the edge of Manasseh’s land were Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo and Dor, with their villages. Joseph’s descendants lived in these towns. Joseph was a son of Israel.{x}
Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi and Beriah were born to Asher, along with a girl named Serah.{y}
From Beriah came Heber and Malchiel. Malchiel founded the town of Birzaith.{z}
Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer and Hotham, and of a girl, Shua.{aa}
Japhlet had three boys: Pasach, Bimhal and Ashvath.{ab}
Born to Shemer were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah and Aram.{ac}
His brother Helem had four sons: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh and Amal.{ad}
From Zophah came Suah, Harnepher and Shual, then Beri and Imrah,{ae}
then Bezer, Hod and Shamma, then Shilshah, Ithran and Beera.{af}
Jether had three sons: Jephunneh, Pispa and Ara.{ag}
Ulla had three sons: Arah, Hanniel and Rizia.{ah}
Every one of these came from Asher. They were family leaders, the finest soldiers, and top commanders. Their records counted 26,000 men ready for battle.

notes.text: Tola means “worm,” a source of red dye. Puah may mean “red dye plant.” Jashub means “he returns.” Shimron means “watch.”
Jeriel means “God founded.” Ibsam means “sweet smell.” Shemuel is the same name as Samuel.
The Hebrew says “sons” of Uzzi. Izrahiah means “Yahweh shines.” Isshiah means “Yahweh lends.”
Lists of Benjamin’s sons are not the same in Genesis 46:21, Numbers 26:38-41 and 8:1-5. Becher means “young camel.” Jediael means “known by God.”
Jerimoth means “heights.” Iri may mean “my city.”
Zemirah means “song.” Eliezer means “my God is help.”
The Hebrew says “sons” of Jediael. Ehud may mean “united.” Zethan means “olive tree.” Ahishahar means “brother of the dawn.”

The Hebrew says “sons” of Aher. Shuppim and Huppim may mean “snakes” and “coverings.” Hushim means “quick ones.” Aher means “another.” Some think this verse once listed Dan’s family (compare Genesis 46:23).
Genesis 46:24 has Jahzeel and Shillem. Jahziel means “God divides.” Jezer means “plan.” Bilhah was Rachel’s servant (Genesis 30:3-8).
The Hebrew of verses 14-15 is hard to follow. Asriel means “God has bound.” Aram is Syria.
Numbers 26:33 makes Zelophehad Machir’s great-grandson. The Hebrew here also mentions “the second,” with no clear link.
Peresh may mean “separation.” Sheresh means “root.” Ulam may mean “first.”
The Hebrew says “sons” of Ulam. Bedan may mean “son of judgment.”
Hammolecheth means “the queen.” Ishhod means “man of glory.” Abiezer means “my father is help.” Mahlah may mean “dancer.”
Shemida means “the name knows.” Ahian means “brotherly.” Likhi means “learned.” Aniam means “I am a people.”
Bered means “hail.” Eleadah means “God has decorated.”
Gath, meaning “winepress,” was a Philistine city. Elead means “God has given witness.” This raid seems to happen while Ephraim was alive (verse 22).
The name Beriah sounds like the Hebrew words for “in trouble.”
Sheerah means “relative.” Uzzen-sheerah means “Sheerah’s point of land.”
Rephah means “riches.” Resheph means “flame.” Telah means “break.” Tahan means “camp.”
Ammihud means “my relative is glory.” Elishama means “my God has heard.”
The Hebrew spells Nun as “Non.” Nun may mean “fish.” Joshua means “Yahweh saves.”
Bethel means “house of God.” Naaran means “young.” Ayyah means “ruin” and may be the town of Ai. Some Hebrew copies read “Gaza.”
Beth-shean means “house of quiet.” Megiddo may mean “place of troops.” Dor means “home.”
Compare Genesis 46:17. Imnah may mean “good luck.” Serah means “plenty.”
Malchiel means “my king is God.” Birzaith may mean “olive well.”
Japhlet means “he rescues.” Shomer, called Shemer in verse 34, means “guard.” Hotham, called Helem in verse 35, means “seal.”
Pasach means “divider.” Bimhal may mean “son of circumcision.”
The Hebrew spells Shemer as “Shamer.” Rohgah means “outcry.” Jehubbah means “hidden.” Some Hebrew copies say “Hubbah.”
Helem may mean “hammer.” Shelesh means “group of three.” Amal means “hard work.”
Harnepher is an Egyptian name that may mean “Horus is good.” Shual means “fox.” Beri means “my well.”
Hod means “glory.” Beera means “well.” Ithran may be the Jether of verse 38.
The meanings of Pispa and Ara are uncertain.
Ulla means “yoke.” Arah means “traveler.” Hanniel means “God’s grace.” Rizia means “delight.”

verses.text: Benjamin’s first son was Bela. Ashbel was born second and Aharah third,{a}
then came Nohah, the fourth, and Rapha, the fifth.{b}
Born to Bela were Addar, Gera and Abihud,{c}
as well as Abishua, Naaman and Ahoah,{d}
and another Gera, along with Shephuphan and Huram.{e}
The following were from Ehud’s family. They led the families living in Geba, but later they were forced to move to Manahath.{f}
They were Naaman, Ahijah and Gera. Gera was the one who led them away.{g} He became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.{h}
Shaharaim had sent away Hushim and Baara, who had been his wives. Afterward, while living in Moab’s country, he fathered more children.{i}
With his wife Hodesh he had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha and Malcam,{j}
and also Jeuz, Sachia and Mirmah. These sons of his became family leaders.{k}
Earlier, Hushim had given him two boys, Abitub and Elpaal.{l}
From Elpaal came Eber, Misham and Shemed. Shemed built the towns of Ono and Lod, along with the villages near them.{m}
Beriah and Shema were leaders of the families settled in Aijalon. They chased away the people living in Gath.{n}
Beriah’s brothers were Ahio, Shashak and Jeremoth.{o}
Beriah’s family included Zebadiah, Arad and Eder,{p}
and also Michael, Ishpah and Joha.{q}
Elpaal’s family included Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki and Heber,{r}
and also Ishmerai, Izliah and Jobab.{s}
Shimei’s family included Jakim, Zichri and Zabdi,{t}
Elienai, Zillethai and Eliel,{u}
and also Adaiah, Beraiah and Shimrath.{v}
Shashak’s family included Ishpan, Eber and Eliel,{w}
Abdon, Zichri and Hanan,{x}
Hananiah, Elam and Anthothijah,{y}
and also Iphdeiah and Penuel.{z}
Jeroham’s family included Shamsherai, Shehariah and Athaliah,{aa}
and also Jaareshiah, Elijah and Zichri.{ab}
All of these were family heads, named as leaders in their family records. They made their homes in Jerusalem.
Jeiel, who founded Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah.{ac}
Abdon was his oldest son. After him came Zur, Kish, Baal and Nadab,{ad}
then Gedor, Ahio and Zecher.{ae}
Mikloth became the father of Shimeah. These families also made their homes in Jerusalem, close to their relatives.{af}
Kish was Ner’s son, and Saul was Kish’s son. Saul’s sons were Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab and Esh-baal.{ag}
Jonathan had a son named Merib-baal, and Merib-baal had a son named Micah.{ah}
Born to Micah were Pithon, Melech, Tarea and Ahaz.{ai}
Ahaz had a son, Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah had Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri. Zimri had a son named Moza.{aj}
Moza had a son, Binea. Next came Raphah, then Eleasah, and then Azel.{ak}
Six sons were born to Azel: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah and Hanan.{al}
Eshek, a brother of Azel, had three boys. Ulam came first, Jeush second, and Eliphelet third.{am}
Ulam’s sons were strong soldiers who could shoot well with bows. They had a great many sons and grandsons, 150 in all. Every one of these came from Benjamin.

notes.text: Compare 7:6-12. Ashbel may mean “man of Baal.” Aharah is called Ehi in Genesis 46:21 and Ahiram in Numbers 26:38.
Nohah means “rest.” Rapha means “he has healed.”
Numbers 26:40 calls Addar “Ard.” Gera means “grain.” Abihud means “my father is glory.” This might also be read “Gera, the father of Ehud” (compare verse 6 and Judges 3:15).
Naaman means “pleasant.” Ahoah means “brotherly.”
Shephuphan means “snake.” Huram means “noble.”
Geba means “hill.” Manahath means “resting place.”
The Hebrew word here can mean “he led them away into exile,” or it can be a name, “Heglam.”
Uzza means “strength.” Ahihud means “brother of glory.”
Shaharaim means “two dawns.” Baara may mean “burning.”
Hodesh means “new moon.” Zibia means “gazelle.” Malcam means “their king.”
Jeuz means “adviser.” Mirmah means “trickery.”
Abitub means “my father is good.” Elpaal means “God is maker.”
Misham means “their cleansing.” Shemed means “destruction.” Lod was later called Lydda (Acts 9:32).
Aijalon means “place of deer.” Gath was a Philistine city.
The Hebrew can be read as names, “Ahio, Shashak,” or as “his brother Shashak.” The Septuagint says “his brothers.”
Zebadiah means “Yahweh has given.” Arad means “wild donkey.” Eder means “flock.”
Ishpah means “bald.” Joha may mean “Yahweh lives.”
Hizki is a short form of Hezekiah.
Ishmerai means “Yahweh guards.” Izliah means “Yahweh pulls out.”
Jakim means “he raises up.” Zichri means “my memory.” Zabdi means “my gift.”
Zillethai means “shadow.”
Beraiah means “Yahweh created.” Shimrath means “guarding.”
Ishpan means “he hides.”
Hanan means “kind.”
Anthothijah means “from Anathoth.”
Iphdeiah means “Yahweh rescues.” Penuel means “face of God.”
Shehariah means “Yahweh is the dawn.” Athaliah means “Yahweh is raised high.”
Elijah means “my God is Yahweh.”
The Hebrew says “the father of Gibeon.” His name, Jeiel, comes from 9:35, where verses 29-38 are repeated. Gibeon means “hill city.”
Kish may mean “bow” or “gift.” The Septuagint and 9:36 add “Ner” after Nadab.
Zecher means “memory.” He is called Zechariah in 9:37.
Mikloth means “staffs.” Shimeah is called Shimeam in 9:38.

Ner means “lamp.” Esh-baal means “man of Baal,” and Baal means “lord” or “master.” In 2 Samuel 2:8 he is called Ish-bosheth, “man of shame.” Writers later put “shame” in place of Baal. 1 Samuel 14:49 lists Ishvi instead.
Merib-baal may mean “Baal fights.” In 2 Samuel 4:4 and 9:6 he is called Mephibosheth.
Melech means “king.” Tarea is called Tahrea in 9:41.
Jehoaddah is called Jarah in 9:42. Azmaveth means “death is strong.”
Raphah is called Rephaiah in 9:43. Azel means “noble.”
Bocheru may mean “his firstborn.” Sheariah means “Yahweh has valued.”
Eshek means “harsh treatment.”

verses.text: Every family in Israel was recorded in the family lists. These lists are written down in the book about the kings of Israel. The people of Judah were taken away as prisoners to Babylon because they had not been faithful to God.{a}
The first ones to move back to their own land and towns were ordinary Israelites, priests, Levites and temple helpers.{b}
Jerusalem became home to some people from Judah and Benjamin, and to some from Ephraim and Manasseh too.{c}
From Judah came Uthai. His father was Ammihud, and before him came Omri, Imri and Bani. They belonged to the family of Perez, Judah’s son.{d}
From the Shilonite clan came Asaiah, the oldest son, together with his sons.{e}
From Zerah’s family came Jeuel. Including his relatives, there were 690 people.{f}
From Benjamin’s tribe came Sallu. His father was Meshullam, and before him came Hodaviah and Hassenuah.{g}

Also from Benjamin came Ibneiah, whose father was Jeroham. There was Elah, whose father was Uzzi and grandfather Michri. And there was Meshullam. His father was Shephatiah, and before him came Reuel and Ibnijah.{h}
The family records listed 956 of their relatives. Each of these men led his own family.
Among the priests were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib and Jachin.{i}
There was also Azariah, the chief officer over God’s house. His father was Hilkiah, and before him came Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth and Ahitub.{j}
There was Adaiah, whose father was Jeroham. Before Jeroham came Pashhur and Malchijah. There was also Maasai, whose father was Adiel. Before Adiel came Jahzerah, Meshullam, Meshillemith and Immer.{k}
Along with their relatives, these priests led families numbering 1,760 men. They were very skilled at the work of serving in God’s house.
Among the Levites was Shemaiah, from Merari’s family. His father was Hasshub, and before him came Azrikam and Hashabiah.{l}
There were Bakbakkar, Heresh and Galal. There was also Mattaniah, whose father was Mica. Mica’s father was Zichri, and Zichri’s father was Asaph.{m}

There was Obadiah, whose father was Shemaiah. Before Shemaiah came Galal and Jeduthun. There was also Berechiah, whose father was Asa and grandfather Elkanah. His home was among the Netophathite villages.{n}
Gate duty belonged to Shallum, Akkub, Talmon and Ahiman, along with men from their families. Shallum was their leader.{o}
Up to that time, these men stood guard at the King’s Gate on the east side. They had been the gatekeepers for the Levite camp.

Shallum was the son of Kore, and before Kore came Ebiasaph and Korah. Shallum and the other men of his family, the Korahites, were in charge of guarding the doorways of the sacred tent. Their ancestors had guarded the entrance to Yahweh’s camp.{p}
In earlier days their leader had been Phinehas son of Eleazar. Yahweh stood with him.
Zechariah son of Meshelemiah guarded the doorway of the tent where God met with his people.{q}
In all, 212 men were picked to guard the doorways. Their names were written in the family lists of their villages. David and Samuel, the prophet who saw visions, had trusted them with this job.
So these men and their descendants watched over the gates of Yahweh’s house, which was the sacred tent. They took turns on guard.
There were guards on all four sides of the building, facing east, west, north and south.
Their relatives who lived in the villages took turns coming in to help them for a week at a time.
But the four head gatekeepers, who were Levites, always stayed on duty. They were trusted to care for the rooms and storerooms of God’s house.
They spent the night stationed around God’s house, because it was their job to guard it. They also held the key and unlocked the doors every morning.
Some Levites took care of the things used in the worship. They counted each item when it was brought in and counted it again when it was taken out.
Others were put in charge of the furniture and the other holy objects. They also looked after the supplies of flour, wine, olive oil, incense and spices.
But only some of the priests blended the spices into perfumed oil.
A Levite named Mattithiah was trusted with baking the flat bread. He was Shallum the Korahite’s oldest son.{r}
Some of their relatives from Kohath’s clan had the job of getting the holy bread ready for each Sabbath day.{s}
Some Levite family heads were singers. They lived in rooms at the temple and were free from other work, because they had to be ready to serve at any hour, day or night.
All of these Levites were family leaders, listed by their family lines. They made their homes in Jerusalem.
Jeiel,{t} who started the town of Gibeon, lived there. Maacah was his wife.
Abdon was his oldest son. After him came Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner and Nadab,
then Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah and Mikloth.
Shimeam was born to Mikloth. These families lived next to their relatives in Jerusalem.
Ner’s son was Kish, and Kish’s son was Saul. Born to Saul were Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab and Esh-baal.
Merib-baal was Jonathan’s son, and Micah was the son of Merib-baal.{u}
Micah had four sons: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea and Ahaz.{v}
Ahaz had a son, Jarah. Jarah’s sons were Alemeth, Azmaveth and Zimri. Moza was born to Zimri.{w}
After Moza came Binea, and after Binea came Rephaiah, Eleasah and Azel, one after the other.
Azel was the father of six boys: Azrikam and Bocheru, Ishmael and Sheariah, and Obadiah and Hanan.{x}

notes.text: The Hebrew can also be read “the book about the kings of Israel and Judah. They were taken away as prisoners.” The Hebrew name for Babylon is Babel.
The Hebrew word for “temple helpers” is Nethinim, meaning “those who are given.” Verses 2-17 are much like Nehemiah 11:3-19.
Jerusalem may mean “foundation of peace.”
Uthai may mean “Yahweh has helped.” Imri means “well spoken.” Perez means “breaking out.”
The Shilonites probably came from Shelah (2:3), not from the town of Shiloh. Asaiah means “Yahweh has made.”
Jeuel may mean “God sweeps away.”
Sallu may mean “weighed.” Hassenuah means “the hated one.”
Ibneiah and Ibnijah both mean “Yahweh builds.” Michri may mean “price paid.” Reuel means “friend of God.”
Jehoiarib means “Yahweh argues the case.” Jachin means “he makes firm.” Compare 24:7, 17.
Nehemiah 11:11 has Seraiah instead of Azariah.
Pashhur may be an Egyptian name. Maasai means “work of Yahweh.” Meshillemith means “payment.” Immer means “lamb.”
Hasshub means “thoughtful.”
Heresh means “craftsman.” Galal means “rolling.” Mattaniah means “gift of Yahweh.”
Jeduthun may mean “praising” (see 16:41). The Netophathites came from Netophah, near Bethlehem.
Talmon may mean “bright.” Ahiman means “my brother is a gift.”
Kore may mean “partridge” or “one who calls.”
Meshelemiah means “Yahweh pays back.”
Mattithiah means “gift of Yahweh.” The flat bread was baked on a griddle (Leviticus 2:5).
The Hebrew says “bread of the rows.” It was the bread set out in rows before Yahweh (Leviticus 24:5-9). Sabbath means “rest.”
This follows the Hebrew note in the margin. The written text has “Jeuel.” Verses 35-44 repeat 8:29-38.
The second time, the Hebrew spells the name “Meri-baal.”
The words “and Ahaz” come from 8:35. They are missing here in the Hebrew.
Jarah means “honeycomb.” He is called Jehoaddah in 8:36.
Compare 8:38.

subheads.2: People Who Came Back to Jerusalem

verses.text: The Philistines went to war against Israel. Israel’s soldiers ran from them, and many were killed on Mount Gilboa.{a}
The Philistine troops pressed in close around Saul and his boys. They cut down Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
The battle turned heavily against Saul. Enemy archers found him with their arrows, and he was badly hurt.

Saul told the young man who carried his weapons, “Take out your sword and kill me. Otherwise these men who don’t know God will come and have fun hurting me.” But the young man was too frightened, and he refused. So Saul took his own sword and threw himself on its point.
When the young man saw that his master had died, he did the same thing. He fell on his own sword and died beside him.
That is how Saul and his three sons died. His whole royal family came to an end together.{b}

Down in the valley, the Israelites learned that their army had scattered and that their king and his sons had fallen. So they deserted their towns and escaped. Then the Philistines came and moved into those towns.
The next morning the Philistines came out to rob the dead. On the slopes of Gilboa they came upon the bodies of Saul and his three sons.
They stripped the armor from Saul’s body and cut off his head. Runners were sent all over their country to carry the news of victory to their idols and their people.
Saul’s armor was put on display in their gods’ temple, and his head was nailed up in Dagon’s temple.{c}
The people of Jabesh in Gilead heard about everything the Philistines had done to Saul.{d}
So all their bravest men went and brought back the bodies of Saul and his sons to Jabesh. They buried the bones beneath the big tree{e} at Jabesh. For a week afterward they fasted and ate nothing.
Saul lost his life because he turned away from Yahweh. He ignored Yahweh’s commands. He even asked a woman who called up the spirits of the dead to guide him,{f}
instead of asking Yahweh. So Yahweh had him killed, and he gave the kingdom to David, Jesse’s son.{g}

notes.text: Verses 1-12 are much like 1 Samuel 31:1-13. Gilboa may mean “bubbling spring.”
1 Samuel 31:6 says his armor carrier and all his men died that day. One son, Esh-baal (also called Ish-bosheth), lived on for a while (8:33; 2 Samuel 2:8).
1 Samuel 31:10 says they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Ashtaroth and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan. Dagon was a Philistine god of grain.
Jabesh means “dry place.” Gilead means “rocky land.”
The Hebrew word means “oak” or another large tree. 1 Samuel 31:13 says “tamarisk tree.”
Jesse means “Yahweh exists” or “gift.”

verses.text: After that, people from every tribe of Israel came together to meet David at Hebron. They told him, “We are your own family. We share the same flesh and blood.{a}

In the past, though Saul was our king, you led our troops out to fight and brought them safely home. Yahweh your God promised you, ‘You will care for my people Israel like a shepherd. You will rule over them.’”

Israel’s leaders all came to King David at Hebron, and there, with Yahweh as witness, he made an agreement with them. Then they poured oil on David’s head to make him Israel’s king. This was what Yahweh had said would happen, through Samuel.{b}
Then David marched with the whole Israelite army to Jerusalem, which was called Jebus at that time. The Jebusite people lived there.{c}
The Jebusites sneered, “You’ll never get inside these walls!” Even so, David seized the mountain fortress of Zion, and from then on it was called David’s City.{d}
Earlier, David had promised, “The first man to strike the Jebusites will become my top army commander.” Joab son of Zeruiah led the attack first, so he got that job.{e}
David made his home inside the fort. That is why people named it the City of David.
He built up the city around the fort, from the Millo all the way around. Joab repaired the rest of Jerusalem.{f}
David grew more and more powerful, because Yahweh of Armies stood by him.{g}
Here are the chief heroes among David’s soldiers. Together with all the people of Israel, they gave David strong support as king, just as Yahweh had promised Israel.{h}
First on the list of David’s heroes was Jashobeam the Hachmonite, head of the Thirty.{i} In one fight he used his spear to kill 300 men.{j}
Next came Eleazar, Dodo’s son, from the Ahohite clan. He was one of the Three, the greatest heroes.{k}
He stood with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. In that place was a field of barley. Israel’s soldiers ran away from the Philistines,{l}
but these heroes planted themselves in the middle of the field and held it. They struck down the Philistines, and Yahweh rescued Israel with a mighty victory.
Once, three of the thirty leaders climbed down the cliff to see David at Adullam Cave. A Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley at the time.{m}
David was staying in his hideout, and some Philistine troops were holding Bethlehem.
David felt very thirsty. He said, “How I wish someone could get me water from the well near Bethlehem’s town gate!”

So the Three slipped through the enemy camp by force. They pulled up water from that well by the gate and carried it all the way back to David. But David refused to drink a drop. Instead, he poured it out on the ground as a gift to Yahweh.

“God forbid that I should drink this!” he said. “These men gambled their lives to fetch it. Drinking it would be the same as drinking their blood.” So he would not drink it. These were the kinds of brave things the Three did.
Joab’s brother Abishai was chief over the Three.{n} He once fought 300 men with his spear and killed them all. He became as famous as the Three.
He was honored twice as much as the other two{o} and became their commander. But he was not counted as one of the Three.

Benaiah, Jehoiada’s son, came from Kabzeel. He was a mighty fighter who did amazing things. He killed two of Moab’s greatest warriors.{p} Another time, on a snowy day, he climbed down into a pit and killed a lion.{q}

He also killed a huge Egyptian who stood seven and a half feet tall.{r} That man’s spear was as heavy as the wooden bar on a weaving loom. Benaiah went at him with only a stick. He yanked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand and killed him with his own weapon.
Such were the mighty acts of Jehoiada’s son Benaiah. His fame grew to match that of the Three.
Among the Thirty he stood out, yet he was never ranked with the Three. David put him in command of the men who guarded the king.
These were the army’s heroes: Joab’s brother Asahel; Dodo’s son Elhanan from Bethlehem;{s}
Shammoth from Harod; Helez from Pelon;{t}
Ira, Ikkesh’s son, a man of Tekoa; Abiezer, a man of Anathoth;{u}
Sibbecai the Hushathite; and Ilai of the Ahohite clan;{v}
Maharai from Netophah; Baanah’s son Heled, also from Netophah;{w}
Ribai’s son Ithai from Gibeah in Benjamin; Benaiah from Pirathon;{x}
Hurai, who came from the streams near Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;{y}
Azmaveth the Baharumite; and Eliahba of Shaalbon;{z}
the sons of Hashem from Gizon; Shagee’s son Jonathan from Harar;{aa}
Sachar’s son Ahiam from Harar; Ur’s son Eliphal;{ab}
Hepher from Mecherah; Ahijah from Pelon;{ac}
Hezro the Carmelite; Naarai, Ezbai’s son;{ad}
Joel, the brother of Nathan; Mibhar, Hagri’s son;{ae}
Zelek, a man of Ammon; Naharai the Berothite, who carried the weapons of Joab son of Zeruiah;{af}
Ira and Gareb, both from the Ithrite clan;{ag}
Uriah the Hittite; Ahlai’s son Zabad;{ah}
Shiza’s son Adina, a leader of Reuben’s tribe, with his thirty men;{ai}
Maacah’s son Hanan; Joshaphat from Mithnah;{aj}
Uzzia the Ashterathite; Hotham’s sons Shama and Jeiel, men of Aroer;{ak}
Shimri’s sons, Jediael and his brother Joha, from Tiz;{al}
Eliel from Mahav; Jeribai and Joshaviah, Elnaam’s sons; Ithmah the Moabite;{am}
and finally Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel from Zobah.{an}

notes.text: Verses 1-9 are much like 2 Samuel 5:1-10. Chronicles skips the seven years when David ruled only Judah (2 Samuel 2-4).
See 1 Samuel 16:1-13.
Jebus may mean “trampled down.” 2 Samuel 5:6 says “the king and his men.”
Zion may mean “fortress.”
Joab means “Yahweh is father.” Zeruiah was David’s sister (2:16).
Millo means “filling.” It was probably a raised stone platform or wall.
The Hebrew is Yahweh Tseba’oth, often translated “the Lord of hosts.” It shows Yahweh as commander of the armies of heaven and of Israel.
Verses 10-41 are much like 2 Samuel 23:8-39. Verses 42-47 are found only here.
Some Hebrew copies say “the officers.” 2 Samuel 23:8 calls him Josheb-basshebeth and “chief of the Three.” Jashobeam means “the people will return.”
2 Samuel 23:8 says 800 men.
Dodo means “his loved one.” The Ahohites came from Ahoah (8:4).
