Riches and honor flow from you. You are Lord of all. Strength and power are in your hands. You can make anyone great and give strength to all.
Our God, we bring you our thanks right now. We praise your wonderful name.
“But who am I, and who are my people, that we could give so freely like this? Everything comes from you. We have only given back to you what you first gave us.
To you, we are like strangers and visitors passing through, just as our ancestors were. Our days here slip past like a passing shadow. Nothing on earth lasts.{j}
Yahweh our God, we have gathered all these riches to build a house for you, to honor your holy name. But all of it came from you. Every bit of it is yours already.

My God, I know that you test our hearts. You are pleased when people are honest and true. I have given all these things gladly and with an honest heart. And now I have watched your people here give to you gladly, and it has filled me with joy.
Yahweh, the God whom Abraham, Isaac and Israel worshiped, always keep this eager love alive within your people. Keep their hearts loyal to you.

Give my son Solomon a heart that truly wants to obey your commands, your teachings and your rules. Help him do everything they say. Help him build this great house that I have gathered all these things for.”

Then David told all the people gathered there, “Now praise Yahweh your God!” So they all praised Yahweh, the God their fathers had worshiped. They bowed low and kneeled before Yahweh and before the king.{k}

On the following day they sacrificed animals to Yahweh. They brought him burnt offerings: one thousand bulls, one thousand rams and one thousand young male sheep. They also poured out drink offerings and brought many other sacrifices for all the people of Israel.

That day they ate and drank in Yahweh’s presence and were very happy. Then for the second time they crowned Solomon, David’s son, as their king. They poured oil on him to set him apart for Yahweh as ruler, and they did the same for Zadok to be priest.{l}
So Solomon took his seat on Yahweh’s throne as king after his father David. He did very well, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the officials and the heroes, and every one of King David’s sons too, promised to be loyal to King Solomon.{m}
Yahweh raised Solomon to great honor while all Israel watched. He gave him royal glory beyond that of any king of Israel before him.
That is how Jesse’s son David came to rule the whole nation of Israel.
For forty years he reigned over Israel. He ruled seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.{n}
He died at a ripe old age after a long life, rich and honored. His son Solomon took the throne after him.
King David’s acts, from first to last, are recorded in the writings of three men: the seer Samuel, the prophet Nathan, and Gad, who was also a seer.{o}
These records describe his reign and his mighty deeds. They describe the events that swept over him and over Israel, and over the kingdoms of every land around them.

notes.text: The Hebrew word for “great building,” birah, can mean “fortress” or “palace.” Here it is used for the temple.
The names of some of these stones are not certain. “Shiny black stones” translates a word used for black eye paint. It may mean a dark stone for decoration.
The Hebrew says “3,000 talents of gold” and “7,000 talents of pure silver.” Ophir was a land famous for its gold, perhaps in southern Arabia or east Africa.
The Hebrew says “to fill his hand,” a way of saying “to set himself apart.”
The Hebrew says “10,000 darics.” A daric was a Persian gold coin first made around 515 B.C. The writer is giving the value in the money used in his own day. Some think it means drachmas.
The Hebrew says “5,000 talents” of gold, “10,000 talents” of silver, “18,000 talents” of bronze and “100,000 talents” of iron.
Jehiel is named in 23:8.
Verses 10-13 are often called David’s prayer. The words of praise added to the Lord’s Prayer in some later copies of Matthew 6:13 sound like verse 11.
Or “You are lifted high as head over all.”
Or “and there is no hope.”
Bowing before the king was a way of showing respect, not worship. The same Hebrew word is used for both.
“The second time” points back to 23:1. Compare 1 Kings 1:32-40, where Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon.
The Hebrew says “gave a hand under Solomon.”
2 Samuel 5:4-5 and 1 Kings 2:11 say he ruled seven years and six months in Hebron.
The Hebrew says “the words of Samuel the seer.” These may be the books of Samuel or other records kept by prophets.
